question: Which of the following phenomena can be explained by “two points determine a line”?
solution: The two nails correspond to two points. Since the line through two points is unique, the wooden strip is fixed in place. The other examples are applications of “the line segment between two points is the shortest path” and “the perpendicular segment is the shortest.”

edges.reason: The point-traces-a-line view is a useful conceptual entry point. Endpoints and unlimited extension suffice to distinguish and draw a line, ray and segment, without surface/solid generation.
edges.scope: conceptual view of lines as traced paths

edges.reason: The two basic facts are statements about lines and segments; these objects must be distinguished.
Vertical-angle equality explains why all four intersection angles are right once one is right. The perpendicular definition and set-square construction do not require that proof.
edges.scope: deducing all four angles are right

edges.reason: The later perpendicular-line node restates the same right-angle intersection definition and adds construction/formal notation. Earlier everyday recognition is useful exposure rather than a distinct required concept.
Perpendicularity is defined by a right angle at an intersection; angle and right-angle meanings are needed.
edges.scope: definition via right angle at intersection

edges.reason: Point-to-point shortest-distance language is a helpful model, but perpendicular-shortest distance is a separate fact and not derived merely from the two-point line axiom.
The distance in question is the length of the perpendicular from the point, so perpendicularity identifies which segment is measured.
